name: FD.io VPP (Vector Packet Processing)
what_it_is: VPP is Cisco's open-source high-performance packet-processing stack that runs on commodity CPUs using a vector-based processing model. It provides production-grade switch/router functionality via a plugin-based, extensible dataplane.
components: vnet — VPP networking layer (L2/L3/L4 forwarding, interface management)
vppinfra — core utilities and data structures
src/plugins — bundled plugin directory (ACL, NAT, DPDK, nsim, perfmon, etc.)
extras/libmemif — client library for memif shared-memory interface
src/vcl — VCL (VPP Communications Library) for host-stack bypass
measurement: statseg — shared-memory statistics segment (per-node counters, interface stats); scrape interval configurable
Prometheus exporter — prom plugin exposes statseg data at an HTTP endpoint (experimental)
IPFIX / flowprobe — exports L2/L3/L4 flow records to a collector
perfmon plugin — per-thread CPU performance counters (PMU-based)
API trace — binary API call tracing (on by default, circular buffer)
BFD stats — forwarding path liveness metrics
configuration: startup.conf — primary configuration file; sections: unix, cpu, dpdk, buffers, plugins, statseg, memory, logging, socksvr, api-trace, api-segment, l3fib, l2fib, ipsec
CLI over UNIX socket (/run/vpp/cli.sock) or interactive terminal
Binary API socket (socksvr default) — used by VPP agents and the VAT test tool
Plugin enable/disable via plugins {} stanza in startup.conf
CPU pinning: main-core, corelist-workers, workers, skip-cores, scheduler-policy (fifo/rr/other)
DPDK device whitelist/blacklist by PCI address; per-device rx/tx queues, TSO, RSS
Hugepage / memory configuration: main-heap-size, page-size, buffers-per-numa
fault_injection: nsim plugin (Network Delay Simulator) — introduces configurable per-interface delay (e.g. 'set nsim delay 20 ms bandwidth 1 gbit packet-size 128') and packet loss fraction (drop-fraction 0.0–1.0)
Packet generator (pg) — high-speed traffic injection into arbitrary graph nodes; supports pcap replay and multi-thread generation; used extensively in make test
modes: Daemon mode (default, nodaemon suppressed in startup.conf)
Worker-thread / multi-core mode (1 main thread + N worker threads pinned to cores)
Container mode (Dockerfiles in extras/docker for bionic/centos7/xenial, build and runtime variants)
DPDK dataplane mode vs. non-DPDK mode (DPDK plugin optional)
constraints: Requires privileged access and hugepages for DPDK dataplane operation; falls back to reduced buffer count (8192) when running unprivileged
Worker threads each require dedicated /dev/shm space; testing requires remounting /dev/shm (empirically ≥2048 MB for 16 cores)
DPDK UIO drivers (vfio-pci, igb_uio, uio_pci_generic) must be loaded before VPP starts — not handled automatically
No docker-compose file is present in the repository; containerised deployments require manual orchestration using the provided Dockerfiles
Prometheus exporter (prom plugin) is marked experimental, not production-ready
nsim drop-fraction and delay apply per-interface and require explicit CLI enablement per interface (nsim output-feature enable-disable <if>)
docker_services: extras/kube-test/docker — kube-test images: base, vpp, nginx, ab, wrk
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml (or equivalent) — the repo ships only individual Dockerfiles; multi-container topologies must be assembled externally
No built-in traffic replay beyond pcap-via-pg; no NAT64 support listed in feature set
Prometheus plugin is experimental with no stable scrape guarantees
